solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chippy’s board left off fish

indicators.note: something left off is omitted, so one word's letters are taken away from the other

blocks.note: chippy is British slang for a carpenter, a worker in wood chips
to board a ship or train is to enter it

explanation.surface: A woodworker's plank has been left out of the fish order at the chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ENTER from CARPENTER leaves CARP; 'Chippy' tempts you towards a fish-and-chip shop, which suits the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The carp is a common freshwater species of the minnow family.

clue.text: One being short of training is a firing offence

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so those letters are missing

blocks.note: one being is a person, with one as the article A
PE is physical education, school exercise training

explanation.surface: Someone without proper training commits a sackable offence at work.
explanation.walkthrough: A PERSON without PE leaves ARSON. 'Firing offence' sounds like grounds for dismissal, but here firing means setting fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property, literally an offence involving fire.

clue.text: Feel aggrieved that map ultimately leads here

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the last letter of the word is kept
to lead is to go in front, so this piece is placed before the other in a down answer

blocks.note: the final letter of map
to resent something is to feel aggrieved by it

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed that the map keeps directing them to this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'here' is hiding at the very end, looking like part of the map's directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Present means in this place, attending, as when a teacher calls the register and pupils answer.

clue.text: Where, finally, to join wild cat safari

definitions.text: Where, finally, to join wild cat safari

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the preceding word, so only its closing letter is used
wild means out of control, so the following letters are scrambled
joining means attaching, so one piece is placed alongside the other

blocks.note: the last letter of where
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks where to sign up for a safari to see big wild cats.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the region of Kenya and Tanzania is where you go on a big-cat safari.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya and Tanzania, in the eastern part of the continent, are the classic destinations for watching lions and leopards in the wild.

clue.text: One charging setter in criminal complaint

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted out of order
charging means rushing into, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter faces criminal charges in court, accused of some wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a legal grievance, but it is the medical sense: an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteritis is an inflammation of the intestine, and a complaint is an everyday word for an ailment or illness.

clue.text: Cakes filled with a hundred wicked things seen here

indicators.note: something filled with an item holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: scones are small baked cakes
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Pastries are stuffed with a hundred naughty treats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' suggests sinful, but it means having a wick: candles are held in these wall brackets.
explanation.definitionFit: A sconce is a wall-mounted bracket holding candles, which are literally objects with wicks.

clue.text: Pale nut found under tree

indicators.note: in a down answer, being under means coming after, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: the ash is a common tree
in printing an en, or nut, is a unit of width

explanation.surface: A colourless nut is picked up beneath a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Printers called the en space a nut, a convention that crosswords borrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face drained of colour, grey like ashes, a synonym for pale.

clue.text: Rifle fire by a parting force

indicators.note: parting something means splitting it, so a piece sits in the gap it opens
by means next to, so the two pieces are placed side by side

blocks.note: RN is the Royal Navy, a fighting force
taken as written
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: Rifle fire tears through a body of troops, splitting it apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Rifle reads as a gun, but it is the verb meaning to search and steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to go through it hurriedly, stealing things, which is to plunder or loot it.

clue.text: Pairs sometimes used to click while dancing

definitions.text: Pairs sometimes used to click while dancing

blocks.clueFragment: Pairs sometimes used to click while dancing
blocks.note: surface reading: dancing couples who get on well together, who click

blocks.clueFragment: Pairs sometimes used to click while dancing
blocks.note: setter's reading: a pair of shell-shaped instruments held in the hand and clicked in time by a flamenco dancer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pairs' suggests couples and 'click' suggests getting on; really these are percussion instruments that come in pairs and make a clicking sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish dancers hold these wooden percussion shells in each hand and snap them together rhythmically.

clue.text: Trifles, possibly about love?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: trifles are an example of puddings, which are called sweets in Britain
love is a score of zero in tennis

explanation.surface: A dessert, perhaps one made for a romantic occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: these are trifles, small unimportant remarks, and they are all about love.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names affectionate words murmured between lovers, pleasing in tone yet trivial in content.

clue.text: Make attractive finish to a queen’s clothing

indicators.note: clothing something wraps it up, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: the finish is the end
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A queen's outfit is given an alluring final touch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen; 'clothing' here is a verb, dressing the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear someone is to make them liked or loved, to render them appealing to others.

clue.text: Clubs and pubs adopting a bright red colour

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the drinking places take a letter between them

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
two kinds of pub, an inn and a bar
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nightclubs and bars are taking on a vivid scarlet decor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like the article of the definition, but it is the letter taken in by the two pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is mercury sulphide ore, whose vivid scarlet shade gives its name to a pigment, vermilion.

clue.text: Cards holding an art patron’s old records

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: aces are playing cards
Henry Tate, the sugar merchant, founded London's Tate gallery; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Greetings cards carry the details of a gallery benefactor's vintage recordings.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Tate, a sugar merchant, gave his art collection to found the Tate gallery in London, so he is the art patron.
explanation.definitionFit: Before tape, studio recordings were cut on discs coated with cellulose acetate, so these discs are early records.

clue.text: He painted lines without a permit

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: a canto is a section of a long poem, made up of lines
taken as written
to permit is to let

explanation.surface: Someone painted road markings without getting official permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it is the old sense of outside; and a canto, a division of a long poem, is a set of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was the eighteenth-century Venetian artist famed for his detailed views of Venice and London.

clue.text: Chain, one that’s six feet, keeping large mammals back

indicators.note: going back means running in the opposite direction, so the letters are read from right to left
keeping something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an insect has six legs, and an ant is one
elk are large deer, and the plural is the same as the singular

explanation.surface: A chained creature six feet tall restrains large beasts that are backing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six feet' sounds like a height, but it means six legs: the ant.
explanation.definitionFit: An anklet is a chain or band worn around the lower leg as jewellery, so a chain fits it.

clue.text: Mimed playing song? It’s caught by screen, briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped
something caught by another is held inside it

blocks.note: an air is a tune or song
a guard, such as a fireguard, is a protective screen
it, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone mimes along to a song, and it is captured briefly on the big screen.
explanation.walkthrough: GUARD loses its D to give GUAR, which then holds IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Air guitar is the pretend strumming of an imaginary instrument while miming along to rock music.

clue.text: Couples decided wearing uniform is retrograde

indicators.note: wearing means having on, which gives the short word for being inside clothes
retrograde means moving backwards, so the string is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: something decided is set, fixed
dressed in something means wearing it
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pairs who have chosen to dress in uniform find it a backward step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couples' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: joins together.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple things is to join or link them, so couples and unites are both verbs of bringing together.

clue.text: Fool left before the end of Satie’s slow movement

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept
before means in front of, so the pieces come in this order

blocks.note: to fool someone is to trick them
L is the abbreviation for left
the final letter of Satie, the French composer

explanation.surface: A joke on the slow movement of a piece by the composer Erik Satie.
explanation.walkthrough: With Satie in the picture, 'slow movement' reads as part of a symphony; it means liquid flowing slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickle is a thin, slow flow of liquid, literally a sluggish movement of water.

clue.text: Noble site bombed first

indicators.note: something bombed is blown apart, so its letters land in a new order

blocks.note: an earl is a nobleman
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's estate was the first to be attacked from the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest is the one coming before all others in time, so it ranks as the initial one.

clue.text: Serious art making money?

blocks.note: first meaning: sincere and solemn in intent
second meaning: in old English, thou art paid becomes thou ..., so art is the archaic second-person 'are', and making money is earning

explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' looks like painting, but it is the old verb form in 'thou art'; the matching old form of earn, said to thou, is spelt the same as the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest describes someone sincere and intense in purpose, a close synonym for serious.

clue.text: One Regan typifies, primarily, in play

definitions.text: One Regan typifies, primarily, in play

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken
letters in play are moved around freely, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written to be rearranged
the first letter of typifies

explanation.surface: Regan in a Shakespeare play is the very model of a certain sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: Regan, the faithless daughter in King Lear, is the play's great example of ingratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, which describes Regan, who turns her father out after he gives her his kingdom.

clue.text: Part of a cathedral made over to relics

indicators.note: something made over is remade into a new form, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A section of a cathedral has been handed over to house holy remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister is the covered walkway around a courtyard that forms part of many cathedrals and monasteries.

clue.text: Course support needed by tense university student

blocks.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
U is the abbreviation for university
on a golf course, a tee is the peg that supports the ball

explanation.surface: An anxious undergraduate needs extra help with their course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a study course, but it is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a person who is being taught by a tutor, a learner under individual instruction.

clue.text: Desperate rebel in southern desert

indicators.note: to desert is to abandon, so these letters walk out of the word

blocks.note: an insurgent is a rebel
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A rebel on the run in the far-south desert is in a desperate plight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like sand dunes, but it is the verb: IN and S abandon INSURGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate need is a pressing one, so desperate and urgent both mean requiring immediate action.

clue.text: Killer allergen in jam sandwiches

indicators.note: the phrase sandwiches the answer, holding it between other letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A deadly allergen is lurking inside jam sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam sandwiches' looks like food, but 'sandwiches' is a verb holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese mercenary trained in stealth and assassination, so a professional killer.

clue.text: Counteract pressure: go by rail, saving seconds

indicators.note: saving something means keeping it safe inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: to travel by rail is to take the train
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: To beat the stress of commuting, travel by train and save time.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the strain is an idiom for bearing a load or supporting weight, resisting a force on something.

clue.text: Broken nose bandaged by top medic

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so its letters are rearranged
something bandaged by another is wrapped in it

blocks.note: to top something is to better it
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken nose is strapped up by the leading doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective for the medic, but it is the verb, to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonesetter sets fractured or dislocated bones; the medic sense fits a traditional healer who treats injuries.

clue.text: Cheese turned out on the counter

indicators.note: counter means in the opposite direction, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: something that turned out was produced, made

explanation.surface: The cheese was put out on the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' looks like the reversal signal, but it gives the letters; the reversing is done by 'on the counter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is the round Dutch cheese with a red wax coat, named after its town of origin.
